record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For every two-qubit state sigma, prove the bi-negativity inequality that the partial transpose, with respect to the second subsystem, of the operator absolute value of sigma’s partial transpose is positive semidefinite: |sigma^{T2}|^{T2} >= 0.

evidence.quote:
A little problem introduced in [AMVW02] is the bi-negativity on two qubits: Prove that
|σT2|T2 ≥ 0
holds for every two-qubit state σ. Here, T2 denotes the partial transpose with respect to the second system (see also problem 2) and √ |.| is the operator absolute value, |x| = x∗ x.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\sigma$ be a density operator (positive semidefinite, trace-one) acting on $\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$. For an operator $X$ on $\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$ written in a product basis as $X = \sum_{ijkl} X_{ij,kl}\, |i\rangle\langle k| \otimes |j\rangle\langle l|$, define the partial transpose with respect to the second subsystem by 
$$X^{T_2} = \sum_{ijkl} X_{ij,kl}\, |i\rangle\langle k| \otimes |l\rangle\langle j|.$$
For any Hermitian operator $Y$, let $|Y| := \sqrt{Y^* Y}$ denote its operator absolute value (i.e., the unique positive semidefinite square root of $Y^*Y$).

Prove or disprove: for every two-qubit state $\sigma$,
$$\bigl|\sigma^{T_2}\bigr|^{T_2} \;\ge\; 0,$$
that is, the partial transpose (with respect to the second subsystem) of the operator absolute value of $\sigma^{T_2}$ is positive semidefinite.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-qubit bi-negativity inequality has been proved. S. Ishizaka established that |σ^{T_2}|^{T_2} ≥ 0 holds for every two-qubit state, and this is recorded as solved on the Open Quantum Information Problems Wiki and used as an established fact in subsequent literature on negativity and entanglement monotones.
